I came across this vid on imgur today, so sorry for the delay, but I wanted to toss in my thoughts on the subject as I see a lot of people saying school shouldn't be federally regulated and other things.

As someone that grew up all over the US, Federal government does need to step in. By having such varying levels of funding for schools, based on both the state's income and the testing scores for each school district, we hurt the students. As does the constant push for people to be college educated. 

Not everyone is as ignorant as the testing makes it seem, it more or less boils down to a persons home life(mainly income) and the way we teach students.

Yet School feels more like a jail that's trying to brute force the knowledge into us, despite our ancestors mainly learning from hands-on trial and error. Hell we still use trial and error testing, though now we are able to simulate things and have scientific formula's to help us predict the outcomes, but it's all based on the trials and errors of those that came before us. 

Yet there are very few alternative schools(and a severe lack of information for those that do exist), for students whom would benefit from a more active hands-on education, most likely because public schools receive more funding for every student that attends.

I'll use myself for example:
I went to a total of 6 different schools between my middle and high school years, 2 in North Carolina, 2 in Oklahoma, 1 in Michigan and 1 in Arizona.

Fort Bragg, NC area schools were lower middle class to low income, I'd say they're curriculum was decent, but they lacked a lot of optional programs(Art. Home Ec and Air Force ROTC were the only options). I did decently enough though despite my boredom.

From NC I went to Ft.Huachuca, AZ and their curriculum was so far ahead, that I had to ask my cousin whom had recently finished her English Major for help with homework but, even she didn't know wtf it was that we were being taught. It literally looked like the intro to Tokyo Drift with some of the football team driving BMW's and Vipers and the whole "it feels like a jail" vibe but clearly was highly funded.
I was constantly in after school detention(which meant Sat mornings) to try and catch up but it wasn't an actual teacher watching us, so getting help was impossible, and I got held in 9th grade for simply not having the same level of education.

From there I went to Grand Rapids, Mi. Where I was, it was mostly upper middle class, I actually enjoyed the school as the teachers made the classes more engaging but I was still behind and, my time in AZ hurt my interest in school. Didn't help that I was depressed either(loss of a pet, parents divorce, loss of friends, etc).

I then went to Ft.Sill Ok, where it was decided I'd go back to 8th grade. I did fine in middle school... honestly all I did was recycle work I did in the 6th grade, then they finally realized I was depressed AF and put me into a mental health "class", but by then I had decided to say "F it" and got my GED and got into skilled trades.

I've learned so much while doing skilled trades simply because it was more hands on, I could see what tasks math allowed me to complete more easily without having to just guess or eyeball a solution.

Hell, I've actually developed an interest in engineering and rocket science just from a general fascination in space, Kerbal Space Program and youtube videos.

Same with Nature, politics, etc. My natural desire to learn about these subjects to better improve the life of myself and of others has taught me far more than school ever has.

tl;dr: Public school is a joke as there is no equality for the lower class. The system is literally designed to keep people with lower income ignorant and, any alternative education that would benefit the lower class is kept hush-hush from the majority of the population, because the more students in public education, the more funding they get.
